Modify the rgba data of pain drawings

Source: R/pdr_modify_rgba.R
pdr_modify_rgba.Rd

Modifies the .rgba array of each pdr_drawing in a pdr_list, e.g. to apply a stencil that restricts a drawing to an anatomical region, or to trim low/high alpha values. It returns a pdr_list of the same length and is thus suited for use inside mutate(). The drawings must already have an .rgba element (see pdr_add_rgba()). See pdr_match() for the definitions of pdr_list and pdr_drawing.

Usage

pdr_modify_rgba(pdr_list, op = "", stencil = NULL, threshold = 0.5)

Arguments

pdr_list

A pdr_list (see pdr_match()) whose pdr_drawings contain .rgba, e.g. the pdr_data column of a pdr_tibble.

op

A string specifying the operation. There is no default (the default "" raises an error); one of:

  • "apply_stencil" — multiplies the alpha channel (4th layer) of .rgba by stencil, so that pixels outside the stencil become fully transparent. Requires stencil.

  • "multiply" — multiplies the whole .rgba array by stencil. Requires stencil.

  • "addition" — unfinished, do not use. Intended to add stencil to the whole .rgba array, but it currently errors and its weighting is still to be decided. Requires stencil.

  • "low_trim" — sets all .rgba values below threshold to 0.

  • "high_trim" — sets all .rgba values above threshold to 1.

stencil

The stencil(s) used by the ops "apply_stencil", "multiply" and "addition"; otherwise ignored. Either

  • a single matrix,

  • a list of matrices, or

  • a pdr_list in which every pdr_drawing has a .stencil element (see pdr_add_stencil()), e.g. pdr_stencil_full_body$pdr_data.

The length must be 1 (the stencil is used for every drawing) or equal to the length of pdr_list (stencils are paired with drawings by position). The height and width of each stencil must match the .rgba of the drawing it is paired with. Default is NULL.

threshold

A number between 0 and 1 used by "low_trim" and "high_trim"; otherwise ignored. Default is 0.5.

Value

A pdr_list of the same length as pdr_list, with modified .rgba elements.

See also

pdr_add_stencil(), pdr_add_rgba(), pdr_plot_stencil()

Examples

# Keep only the pain drawn within the first region of the full body stencils
pdr_example_data[1:2, ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data) |>
      pdr_modify_rgba(
        op = "apply_stencil",
        stencil = pdr_stencil_full_body$pdr_data[1]
      )
  ) |>
  pdr_plot_rgba()


# Remove faint (low alpha) pixels
pdr_example_data[1:2, ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data) |>
      pdr_modify_rgba(op = "low_trim", threshold = 0.3)
  )
